subject: maths
pattern: Application of Derivatives carries 10-12 marks in the Karnataka 2nd PUC maths paper: 1-2 mark questions on rate of change, tangent slope and increasing function, 3-mark questions on intervals of monotonicity, local maxima/minima or tangent and normal, and a compulsory 5-mark word problem on maxima and minima (the cone, the rectangle in a circle, the wire cut into two pieces). Examiners expect first and second derivative tests to be stated with the sign conclusion.

questions.q: Find the rate of change of the area of a circle with respect to its radius $r$ when $r=3$ cm.
Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=x^3-x+1$ at $x=2$.
Write the interval in which $f(x)=x^2$ is strictly increasing.
questions.answer: $f'(x)=2x>0$ for $x>0$. Hence $f$ is strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$.

questions.q: The radius of a circle is increasing at the rate of $0.7$ cm/s. What is the rate of increase of its circumference?
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=x^3$ at the point $(1,1)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2$; at $(1,1)$ the slope is $3$. Equation: $y-1=3(x-1)$, i.e. $3x-y-2=0$.
$f'(x)=3x^2-6x+3=3(x-1)^2$. Since $(x-1)^2\ge0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $f'(x)\ge0$ (and it is zero only at $x=1$). Hence $f$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.q: Using differentials, find the approximate value of $\sqrt{36.6}$.
questions.answer: Let $y=\sqrt x$, $x=36$, $\Delta x=0.6$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}=\dfrac{1}{12}$. $\Delta y\approx\dfrac{dy}{dx}\Delta x=\dfrac{0.6}{12}=0.05$. So $\sqrt{36.6}\approx6+0.05=6.05$.

questions.q: Find the intervals in which $f(x)=2x^3-3x^2-36x+7$ is increasing or decreasing.
questions.answer: $f'(x)=6x^2-6x-36=6(x^2-x-6)=6(x-3)(x+2)$. $f'(x)=0$ at $x=-2,3$, dividing the line into $(-\infty,-2)$, $(-2,3)$, $(3,\infty)$. $f'>0$ on $(-\infty,-2)$ and $(3,\infty)$: increasing. $f'<0$ on $(-2,3)$: decreasing.

questions.q: Find the local maximum and local minimum values of $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+15$.
Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of $f(x)=2x^3-15x^2+36x+1$ on $[1,5]$.
questions.answer: $f'(x)=6x^2-30x+36=6(x-2)(x-3)$, critical points $x=2,3$ both in $[1,5]$. $f(1)=24$, $f(2)=29$, $f(3)=28$, $f(5)=56$. Hence absolute maximum is $56$ at $x=5$ and absolute minimum is $24$ at $x=1$.

questions.q: Find the equations of the tangent and normal to the curve $y=x^2+2$ at the point $(1,3)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x$; slope of tangent at $(1,3)$ is $2$. Tangent: $y-3=2(x-1)$, i.e. $2x-y+1=0$. Slope of normal $=-\dfrac12$. Normal: $y-3=-\dfrac12(x-1)$, i.e. $x+2y-7=0$.

questions.q: A spherical balloon is being inflated so that its volume increases at $900\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. How fast is the radius increasing when the radius is $15$ cm?
questions.answer: $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. Given $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=900$, $r=15$: $900=4\pi(225)\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{900}{900\pi}=\dfrac1\pi$ cm/s.

questions.q: Show that of all the rectangles inscribed in a given fixed circle, the square has the maximum area.
questions.answer: Let the circle have radius $R$ and the rectangle sides $x,y$. Then $x^2+y^2=4R^2$, so $y=\sqrt{4R^2-x^2}$. Area $A=xy$, so $A^2=Z=4R^2x^2-x^4$. $\dfrac{dZ}{dx}=8R^2x-4x^3=0\Rightarrow x^2=2R^2$. $\dfrac{d^2Z}{dx^2}=8R^2-12x^2=-16R^2<0$, so area is maximum. Then $y^2=4R^2-2R^2=2R^2=x^2$, i.e. $x=y$. Hence the rectangle is a square.

questions.q: Show that the right circular cone of least curved surface area and given volume has an altitude equal to $\sqrt2$ times the radius of the base.
questions.answer: Let radius $r$, height $h$, volume $V=\tfrac13\pi r^2h$ (fixed), so $h=\dfrac{3V}{\pi r^2}$. Curved surface $S=\pi r\sqrt{r^2+h^2}$; $S^2=\pi^2r^4+\dfrac{9V^2}{r^2}=Z$. $\dfrac{dZ}{dr}=4\pi^2r^3-\dfrac{18V^2}{r^3}=0\Rightarrow 2\pi^2r^6=9V^2$. Using $V^2=\dfrac{\pi^2r^4h^2}{9}$: $2\pi^2r^6=\pi^2r^4h^2$, so $h^2=2r^2$, $h=\sqrt2\,r$. $\dfrac{d^2Z}{dr^2}=12\pi^2r^2+\dfrac{54V^2}{r^4}>0$, so $S$ is minimum.

questions.q: A wire of length 28 m is to be cut into two pieces. One piece is bent into a square and the other into a circle. What should be the lengths of the two pieces so that the combined area is minimum?
questions.answer: Let the square have side $x$ (piece $4x$); the circle's circumference is $28-4x=2\pi r$, so $r=\dfrac{28-4x}{2\pi}$. Area $A=x^2+\pi r^2=x^2+\dfrac{(28-4x)^2}{4\pi}$. $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=2x-\dfrac{2(28-4x)}{\pi}=0\Rightarrow\pi x=28-4x\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{28}{\pi+4}$. $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=2+\dfrac8\pi>0$, so $A$ is minimum. Square piece $=4x=\dfrac{112}{\pi+4}$ m; circle piece $=28-4x=\dfrac{28\pi}{\pi+4}$ m.
